# Whale sightings {#sec-app-whales}

[Informative]{.status}

Whale sightings were the framework's **proof of concept**.
They are a clear example of real-time situational awareness that current standards do not provide:
a sighting is useful to vessels nearby for minutes to hours, it may come from a mariner, a shore network or an automated detector,
and it needs to reach vessels whether or not they are connected to the internet.

## Flow

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "A sighting from origin to helm (illustrative)."
sequenceDiagram
  participant O as Observer
  participant S as Shore sighting<br/>service
  participant AU as Authority
  participant SH as Shadow of<br/>Vessel B
  participant G as Vessel B<br/>gateway
  participant D as Vessel B<br/>display
  participant A as Vessel A AIS<br/>(AIS only)
  participant DA as Vessel A<br/>display
  O->>S: Report sighting<br/>(IP, signed)
  S->>S: Update the organism<br/>from the sighting
  S->>AU: Notify of sighting (IP)
  AU->>SH: Notice of a zone<br/>around the organism (IP)
  SH->>G: Deliver when<br/>connected (IP)
  G->>D: Present on<br/>chartplotter<br/>(NMEA 2000)
  S->>A: Sighting via shore station<br/>(AIS)
  AU->>A: Notice via shore station<br/>(AIS)
  A->>DA: AIS message<br/>in a PGN<br/>(NMEA 2000)
```

Three Things take part, each with its own identity (@sec-sightings-organisms):
the **sighting**, which the observer originates;
the **organism** it observed, which the sighting service updates from it;
and the **notice**, which the authority issues about the organism.

The sighting and the notice can both reach the helm, and at every step each is **the same Thing**: same identity, same meaning, same provenance —
carried at full fidelity over IP, and over AIS and NMEA 2000 as its changes, without its references (@sec-ais-identity).
A sighting relayed over AIS travels in an Area Notice ASM, but it is still a sighting, not a notice.
